Complete the assignment below, thoroughly:

# Target
`lib/src/tools/builtin_tools.dart` (2797 lines) — the built-in tool registry + implementations. It has NO part files yet; you introduce the pattern here.

# Change
1. Read the file fully and map its cohesive regions (read/truncation machinery, write/edit tools, list/bash/shell-jobs, sqlite/archive/lsp/mcp/web wiring — whatever you actually find).
2. Convert to a `part`-based library: add a library name/doc at top (it may already have one — keep whatever form it has), declare `part 'builtin_tools_<family>.dart';` and move cohesive regions out. Follow the repo's part-file conventions (see lib/src/cli/agent_cli*.dart for naming/style; parts declare `part of 'builtin_tools.dart';` or `part of builtin_tools;` — match how agent_cli parts declare theirs).
3. The public function signatures in the primary file (e.g. `builtinTools(...)` and anything exported/imported by other libraries — check who imports this file: `grep -rn "builtin_tools.dart" lib bin test --include=*.dart | grep import`) must keep working unchanged: parts share the library scope so top-level privates moved out stay visible. Do not change any public signature.
4. Target: primary file < 2000 lines (extract at least ~800 lines); each part < 2000 lines.

# Acceptance
- `wc -l lib/src/tools/builtin_tools.dart` < 2000; no lib/src/tools/builtin_tools*.dart over 2000.
- `dart format` clean on touched files; `dart analyze lib/src/tools` reports no issues.
- `dart analyze` at repo root reports no NEW errors (other agents are editing in parallel — focus on errors in files you touched; note any pre-existing/unrelated ones in your report).
- `dart test test/tools` passes (your area's suite).
